headline: Ranked water service to Eldredge Cemetery as top funding priority; approved memo seeking state exemption for columbaria.
summary: The meeting discussed a planned stormwater and wetland project at Shelburne Road Cemetery, with construction expected in 2028. Water service to Eldredge Cemetery was ranked as the top funding priority. Members approved a memo asking the state for a statute exemption for columbaria.
decisions: Approved a tribute to John Simson for the FY2026 Annual Report unanimously, and approved its submission.
Approved the memo seeking a state statute exemption for columbaria unanimously.
Ranked water service to Eldredge Cemetery as the top funding priority, ahead of fencing at Shelburne Road Cemetery and a columbarium.
Agreed unanimously to remove a paragraph and add a photo to the draft City newsletter article.

plain_text:
Page 1 
Sextons Committee 
October 13 , 2026  
 
The Sexton’s committee held a regular meeting on October 13th, 2026 at 3:00 pm, in 180 
Market Street, 3rd Floor Conference Room 301, and by 
Zoom  https://zoom.us/j/97442869500.  
Members present: Chuck Rainville, Jennifer McClory, Peter Taylor, Richard Thorngren, 
Elise Guyette 
Also present: City Council Liaison Andrew Chalnick; Dan Albrecht and Chris Dubin, 
Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission; Andres Torizzo and Kerri Garvey, 
Watershed Consulting; Katherine King, Vermont DEC; Caroline Foley, City of South 
Burlington.   
1. First item: Meeting called to order at 3:02pm. 
 
2. Second item: motion to add newsletter draft after item 10 approved unanimously.  
 
3. No comments from the public. 
 
4. September 8, 2026, minutes approved unanimously. 
 
5. Update on potential stormwater project at Shelburne Road cemetery by Caroline 
Foley, Stormwater PM, CCRPC, Watershed Consulting, and Vermont DEC. 
Members of CCRPC and Watershed Consulting provided an update on a planned 
watershed phosphorus reduction project in the Shelburne Road cemetery and in 
the gully south of the Nissan Car dealership adjacent to the cemetery. The swale 
located in the Shelburne Road Cemetery is a Class II wetlands, and the project 
would include removal of invasives plants and replanting with native vegetation to 
stabilize the banks and restore the wetlands.  
A new outlet pipe for the wetlands is envisioned as the existing pipe under the 
Nissan dealership parking lot is collapsed and at the end of its life.   
There is opportunity for the City to do the project cooperatively with CCRPC and 
Vermont DEC to extend the invasive plant removal, replace the fencing, or other 
beneficial projects for the cemetery. Soil contamination monitoring in the cemetery
Sexton Committee Metting October 13, 2026 | Page 2 
is ongoing Atlas Technical Consultants, LLC and reports should provide information 
about the water table.  The project anticipates no change to the water table in the 
cemetery. In addition, if existing graves abut the work area that may require an 
archeological survey. The project currently relies on assumed property lines, and 
the project may need a full boundary survey. Timing for construction is expected in 
2028 and may be completed in phases.   
6. Review of the current beautification donation fund accounting. Chuck updated the 
committee that Public Works is lending a pump for watering and Church Hill 
Landscaping provided a $600 credit for using the City provided water for the first 
watering.  The accounting continues the plan for cost associated with water hauling 
as the City has not committed to long term refilling of the water tanks.  The new 
updated available balance for additional beautification is $6,771.75.   
 
7. The committee approved unanimously a tribute to John Simson to be included in 
the Sextons FY2026 Annual Report which with the Track Changes indicated and 
circulated by email in advance was also approved for submission It was agreed that 
the group photo from the FY2025 Annual Report would be included and that 
inclusion of the memorial before and after photos would be urged when submitted. 
 
8. The committee discussed a draft memo to seek municipal exemption in the State 
Statutes for Columbaria. Chuck’s draft will be updated to request an exemption for 
municipal cemeteries with a minimum of size of 1.5 acres or the smallest possible 
change to statute for ease of passage.  It will then be sent to State Rep Kate Nugent 
and State Senator Thomas Chittenden with copies to the City Manager and City 
Council.  The memo with discussed changes and action to share it were approved 
unanimously.   
 
9. The Committee discussed new fencing at Shelburne Road Cemetery, Water Service 
at Eldedge Cemetery, and purchase of a columbaria as the three highest priority 
funding requests. After discussion, requesting water service to Eldredge is the top 
priority due to the new plantings, additional tree plantings planned, and possible 
additional planting elsewhere in the cemetery.   
 
A columbarium is on hold as a priority while they are not permitted in cemeteries 
under five acres by State statute and the market for niches in South Burlington is 
unknown. Fencing could happen in conjunction with the wetland improvement 
project and requires the Nissan dealership to avoid plowing their snow into the 
cemetery fence.  Committee members will also attend the joint City Council
Sexton Committee Metting October 13, 2026 | Page 3 
Planning Commission meeting to advocate for land purchase near the cemetery for 
City open space and potentially a new access drive from Fayette Drive.   
 
10. Chuck met with City Communications and Outreach Manager Andy Brumbaugh to 
discuss new cemetery name and rules signage. Chuck proposed to have him on 
the November agenda to discuss size, fonts, colors, etc.  Andy and Chuck suggest 
the name sign and rules sign be separated so that rules can be changed if needed.   
 
11. Under other business the committee reviewed the draft article for the City 
newsletter.  It was agreed unanimously to remove the last paragraph about the 
open Sextons Committee position and to add a photo of the new plantings. It was 
agreed that the article and photo should also be sent to The Other Paper.  
 
Peter requested we complete the City survey about budget priorities.   
 
Chuck updated the committee on the three possible locations discussed with John 
Simson’s family for a memorial bench.  Before final locations are determined, 
ground penetrating radar is required to confirm no graves are present. The 
committee is asked to consider what rules or guidelines we want to put in place 
around materials acceptable for memorial benches.   
 
12. At the conclusion of other business, the meeting was adjourned at 4:45PM.
